To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have successfully applied the dynamical coupled‐ channel approach based on the hadronic Julich πN interaction model to pion photoproduc‐ tion.

we are able to reproduce the experimental data for the differential cross section and the photon spin asymmetry for the reactions γn→π+n and γp→π−p in the resonance region with the same set of free parameters that are also used to describe πN→π+N scattering.

the coupled‐channel model with a realistic treatment of the πN interaction is capable of providing a good description of all the pion photoprocesses in the region of the Δ(1232) resonance and above, including the γn→π0n reaction.

the present dynamical coupled‐channels approach is a very useful and powerful tool in the investigation of pion photoproduc­tion reactions in the resonance region.
the present coupled‐channel model provides a consistent description for the πN→ππN reactions, including the pion photoproductions.

this model is able to describe the pion photoproduc‐tion data up to 1 GeV center‐ of‐mass energy, and that it provides a unified description of the pion photopro‐duction and pion‐nucleon scattering processes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dynamical coupled‐channels approach is able to reproduce the data with a single set of free parameters, without any additional ad hoc assumptions.
the inclusion of the ρN effective channel is crucial for an adequate description of the data.
